sections.content:
You know *por eso* from A2 Unit 5, and *entonces* from A1. This lesson gives you three ways to draw a conclusion.

• *así pues*: "so", "then". It sums up an argument and starts a new sentence, with a comma after it. It is a little formal.
• *entonces*: "so", "then". In conversation it draws a conclusion from what the other person has just said.
• *de ahí que*: "that is why", "hence". It points back at a fact you have just stated and says what follows from it.

After *de ahí que* the verb is in the subjunctive, in the present or, for the past, in the imperfect (B1 Unit 4). That is the difference from *por eso*, which takes the indicative.

sections.title: Same result, two connectors
rows: Hay mucho tráfico; por eso mucha gente va en bicicleta.
There is a lot of traffic; that is why a lot of people cycle.
Hay mucho tráfico; de ahí que mucha gente vaya en bicicleta.
There is a lot of traffic; hence a lot of people cycle.
La película era larga; de ahí que muchos se fueran antes del final.
The film was long; hence many people left before the end.

items.spanish: El plan es caro y no hay tiempo. Así pues, buscamos otra solución.
items.english: The plan is expensive and there is no time. So, we are looking for another solution.
"It is very cold." "Then we stay inside."

sections.content: *De ahí que* is never followed by the indicative: *de ahí que va* is a mistake, *de ahí que vaya* is right.
